app.title: Nagar Seva
app.footer: Built as a final-year project · English + Hindi · Times shown in IST

landing.h1: Report a civic problem. We route it to the right team.
landing.sub: Write in English or Hindi. Our system understands the problem, picks the department, rates how urgent it is, and keeps you updated until it is fixed.
landing.howTitle: From your phone to the right desk in seconds
landing.s1d: Type in English or Hindi, drop a pin on the map and add a photo if you can.
landing.s2d: The system finds the category, the department and how urgent it is, and shows you why.
landing.s3d: The right officer is assigned. You follow every step and confirm when it is really fixed.
landing.t1d: If the system is not sure, or the problem is dangerous, a person decides. Nothing risky is auto-routed.
landing.t2d: Every priority comes with a points breakdown: category, danger words, location, duration and repeat reports.
landing.t3d: Only you, the assigned officer and the admin can see your complaint. Passwords are stored hashed.
landing.finalSub: Creating an account takes under a minute.
landing.rolesTitle: Three kinds of users, three separate doors
landing.rolesSub: Everyone uses the same system but sees different screens. Pick the one that describes you.

guide.link: How to use this portal (user guide)
guide.title: How to use Nagar Seva
guide.intro: Nagar Seva helps you report everyday civic problems such as potholes, garbage or water leaks. This page explains who does what and how to use each screen, step by step.
guide.pickHint: Use the cards above to switch between the three roles.

who.citizen: You report a problem and follow it until it is fixed. Anyone can create a citizen account.
who.officer: You fix the problems assigned to you. Your account is given by the administration.
who.admin: You supervise: you decide doubtful complaints, fix wrong locations and watch the numbers. Your account is given by the project team.

citizen.title: For citizens: how to report a problem

steps.d: Click Sign up. Enter your name, email and a password of at least 8 characters. A mobile number is optional; only the admin can see it.
After logging in you land on the report form. You can write in English or Hindi.
Say what is wrong, where, and for how long. Mention anything dangerous, for example children or an open hole. Example: Big pothole outside the school gate, bikes slipping for 3 days.
Click the map to drop a pin, or press Use my location. The map shows the address it found; press Use this as my address if it is right. You can also type the address yourself.
A clear photo helps the officer. JPG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB. If the photo has its location saved, we can compare it with your pin.
Press Preview to see the category, department and priority the system suggests. Then press Submit.
Open My complaints. Click Details to see the priority points, the officer and the history of every step.
When the officer marks it Resolved, check the place. If it is fixed, confirm and rate it. If not, reopen it and tell us what is still wrong.

tips: One complaint per problem, with a clear place.
Write the real danger (children, traffic, water, fire). It raises the priority honestly.
If the pin is wrong, click the map again before you submit.

officer.title: For officers: how to handle a complaint

steps.d: Use the Officer tab on the login page. Your account is created by the administration.
You see complaints for your department and ward, with the most urgent first. The coloured bar shows priority.
Click Details to see why it got this priority, the address, the photo and the history.
Press Start work so the citizen knows someone is on it.
Press Location is wrong. The admin will correct the pin.

steps.t: If you cannot find the place
steps.d: Press I cannot find the place and write the difficulty. The admin can reply and may share the citizen's phone number for this one complaint.
When done, write what you did and press Resolve. The citizen then confirms or reopens.

tips: The citizen's phone number is visible only if the admin shares it, and only while the complaint is open.
Use the note to say exactly what was done; the citizen reads it.
Critical complaints are shown first; handle them before others.

admin.title: For admins: how to supervise

steps.d: Use the Admin tab on the login page.
Complaints the system was unsure about, or that are dangerous, wait here. Choose the right category; the department follows automatically.
Complaints with a doubtful pin appear here. Click the correct place on the map and save. Priority is recalculated.
When an officer cannot find a place, reply with a message. You may tick the box to share the citizen's phone number for that complaint; this is recorded.
Fake, duplicate or unreachable complaints can be rejected with a reason. The record is kept and the citizen sees the reason.
See totals, resolution rate, busiest areas and how often the system routed automatically.
Change which department handles each category. No retraining is needed.

tips: Each routing decision you make is saved and can later improve the model.
Share a phone number only when it is really needed.

status.in_review: The system was not sure, or the case is dangerous. The admin is deciding where it goes.
status.assigned: Sent to a department and an officer. Work has not started.
status.in_progress: The officer is working on it.
status.resolved: The officer says it is fixed. Waiting for the citizen to confirm.
status.reopened: The citizen said it is not fixed. Back with the officer.
status.closed: The citizen confirmed the fix. Finished.
status.rejected: The admin could not accept this complaint. The reason is in the history.

guide.prioIntro: Priority is a score built from the type of problem, danger words, nearby schools or hospitals, how long it has lasted and repeated reports. You can see every point in Details.

priorities.d: Affects daily life; should be handled soon.
Risk to health or safety, or a main road, school or hospital area.
Immediate danger, for example an open manhole. A person always looks at these first.

faq.a: You, the officer assigned to it, and the admin. Other citizens cannot.

faq.q: Why did my complaint go to review?
faq.a: The system was not sure enough, the problem looked dangerous, or it was marked Other. A person then decides, which is the safe choice.

faq.q: Do I have to give my phone number?
faq.a: No, it is optional. If you give it, only the admin sees it, and an officer sees it only if the admin shares it for one complaint.
Password reset by email is not available yet. If you are logged in you can change it on your Profile page; otherwise ask the administration.

faq.q: I put the pin in the wrong place.
faq.a: Before submitting, click the map again. After submitting, the officer or admin can correct the location.

faq.q: Why is the time shown differently?
faq.a: All times are shown in Indian Standard Time.
